text: No more than two people may ride on a motorcycle, excluding anyone in an attached sidecar.
A passenger may only be carried if the motorcycle's engine exceeds 50cc, and the passenger must be seated in a sidecar or astride a pillion.
No more than two adults may be carried in a sidecar attached to a motorcycle.
Neither the rider nor passenger may take hold of another vehicle that is in motion.
All wheels of the motorcycle must stay in contact with the road surface at all times.

A person may not drive a motor vehicle of a prescribed class without a professional driving permit (kept with them in the vehicle), except a learner accompanied by someone registered as a professional driver for that class.
A vehicle may not be operated on a public road in a manner that causes excessive noise.
Riders must travel in single file within the same lane, except briefly to overtake another motorcycle; two motorcycles may not overtake another vehicle at the same time.
A sidecar must be attached to the left side of the motorcycle, and may not be fitted to a motorcycle with an engine under 50cc.
A driver must yield right of way, slow down, or stop for a pedestrian crossing a roadway within a pedestrian crossing.
A driver may not pass a vehicle that has stopped at a pedestrian crossing.

Pedestrians may not cross while the red man light is showing; if the red man flashes, pedestrians already in the road must finish crossing quickly, while those not yet in the road must wait for the green man.
A vehicle left in the same place for more than 24 hours (outside an urban area) or 7 days (within an urban area) is deemed abandoned by its owner.

Don't cause a vehicle's wheel to drag or spin on the roadway (except in an emergency), use chocks or shoes between a moving wheel and the road surface, or otherwise use or move a vehicle in a way that damages the road.

Animal-drawn vehicles, pedal cycles, motorcycles under 50cc or electrically propelled, motor quadrucycles, disability vehicles under 230kg, and tractors (outside road construction or maintenance use) may not use a freeway.
A parking brake is a brake, normally a hand brake, used to keep a vehicle stationary.
The towed vehicle's steering must be controlled by a person licensed to drive that class of vehicle.
If the towed vehicle's brakes don't comply with requirements, it must be connected by a draw-bar or tow-bar rather than a rope or chain.
A drawing vehicle may tow a maximum of two trailers, or one other motor vehicle that isn't a trailer.
In an emergency, it is permitted to tow one other motor vehicle (not a trailer) together with a trailer.
Don't cross or enter a public road unless it's clear of moving traffic for a sufficient distance, or you can do so with safety to yourself and other traffic.
A light motor vehicle's tyres must show a clearly visible tread pattern across the full breadth and circumference, at least 1mm deep.

A light motor vehicle may not drive on the shoulder of a public road, except between sunrise and sunset, while being overtaken on a single-lane-each-way road, if it can be done safely, and if visibility is at least 150 metres.

Passing on the left is allowed, if it can be done safely, when the vehicle ahead is turning right or has signalled to; on a one-way urban road wide enough for two or more lanes; on an urban road wide enough for two or more lanes each way; where signs designate lanes on a one-way road; or under a traffic officer's direction.
At a junction where vehicles must move around a traffic island, give way to all traffic approaching from your right, unless a traffic officer or road sign directs you otherwise.

Don't park where a traffic officer directs otherwise, in contravention of a sign, where stopping isn't permitted, where the vehicle would obscure a road sign, on the sidewalk, or blocking a private or public vehicular entrance.

Don't stop alongside or opposite an excavation or obstruction if it would obstruct or endanger traffic, in a tunnel, subway, or on a bridge (or within 6 metres of one), where the roadway has been narrowed (or within 6 metres of the narrowing), in contravention of a sign, facing oncoming traffic on the right side, alongside another vehicle on a road under 9 metres wide, within a railway level crossing, within 9 metres of a pedestrian crossing's approach side, or anywhere it would endanger or obstruct traffic.
Don't let the engine emit abnormal smoke or fumes, run while the vehicle is stationary and unattended, or run while fuel is being delivered into the tank.
A rider may not carry a person, animal, or bulky object in front of them; a non-bulky object may be carried if securely attached and doesn't obstruct the rider's view or control.
Don't stop on a freeway except by sign or traffic officer direction, in a designated stopping/parking area, or for reasons beyond your control.

Stop as directed by a road traffic sign or a uniformed traffic officer, at the request or signal of a person leading livestock (cattle, horse, donkey, mule, sheep, goat, pig, or ostrich), or when animals are crossing the road -- only proceeding once all have crossed and it's safe.
Don't drive, or occupy the driver's seat with the engine running, while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a narcotic drug.

A heavy motor vehicle may not be used if its fuel tank, carburettor, or fuel pipes are defective or exposed as a danger, if the fuel tank lacks an effective cap, or if the electrical wiring and battery aren't properly installed, insulated, and maintained.
A junction is the portion of an intersection within the lateral limits of the intersecting roadways, including any stop or yield line marking painted there.

A professional driver drives a motor vehicle of a prescribed class and must hold a professional driving permit; this doesn't apply to a learner accompanied by a registered professional driver for that class.
A vehicle is a device designed mainly to travel on wheels or crawler tracks (excluding devices that move solely on rails).
Don't drive, pull, or push a vehicle on a sidewalk.

A Code 2 learner's licence authorises driving any motor vehicle or combination (other than a motorcycle or tricycle) with tare, GVM, or GCM not exceeding 3500kg, only under the direct supervision of a licensed driver for that class. Minimum age is 17; valid for 24 months from the test date.

A Code 3 learner's licence authorises driving any motor vehicle or combination (other than a motorcycle, tricycle, or quadrucycle) -- covering both light and heavy vehicles -- only under the direct supervision of a licensed driver for that class. Minimum age is 18; valid for 24 months from the test date.
A motorcycle's lamps must be undamaged, properly secured, and capable of being lit at all times.
To 'stop' means to bring a vehicle to a standstill.
Dip your main beam for oncoming traffic, and when following another vehicle.
Every headlamp on dipped beam must adequately illuminate the road ahead, enabling the driver to see a person, vehicle, or substantial object at least 45 metres away.
A vehicle may not be driven in motion using only its parking lamps.
A motorcycle or motor tricycle must be fitted with a rear lamp emitting red light.
A light motor vehicle must be fitted with rear lamps emitting red light.
A heavy motor vehicle must be fitted with at least one rear lamp on each side emitting red light.
A light motor vehicle or motorcycle must have rear stop lamps that emit a red light brighter than the rear lamps, visible at 30 metres in normal sunlight.
A heavy motor vehicle must have at least one stop lamp on each side at the rear, meeting the same brightness and visibility requirements.
An illuminated stop lamp indicates the vehicle is decreasing speed and may stop.
A vehicle must have at least one number-plate lamp at the rear, making every letter and figure on the plate visible from 20 metres by a person of normal eyesight.
A number plate must be SABS-approved and fitted so it cannot easily be detached.
A number plate must be upright (or within 30 degrees), with every letter and figure clearly legible and the whole plate visible.
Motorcycles, motor tricycles, and trailers need only a rear number plate; all other motor vehicles need one at the front and one at the rear.
Fog lamps may only be lit in conditions of poor visibility caused by snow, fog, mist, dust, or smoke.
A driver must have a full, clear view of the road ahead, and to the left and right, while the vehicle is in use.
A light or heavy motor vehicle's steering gear must be maintained in a condition that allows the vehicle to be steered safely and efficiently.
The tow-rope, chain, or tow-bar between two vehicles may not exceed 3.5 metres in length.
A motorcycle must have two independent, working braking systems -- one acting on the front wheel, one on the rear wheel(s).
A light or heavy motor vehicle must be equipped with a working service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake (the emergency and parking brake may be one and the same).
A hooter may only be used when necessary on the grounds of safety.
A light motor vehicle must have a working hooter, audible by a person of normal hearing from 90 metres.
A tune-playing siren or horn may not be used on a private vehicle.
A driver must immediately give way to any emergency vehicle sounding a siren and displaying warning lights.

Emergency vehicles include fire-fighting, rescue, and emergency medical/ambulance vehicles (red light), a vehicle driven by a traffic officer on duty (blue light), and a vehicle engaged in civil protection (green light).
Seatbelts are compulsory for children and adults aged 3 and older while the vehicle is moving forward.
If seatbelts are fitted, rear-seat passengers must wear them while the vehicle is being driven.
A child is defined as aged 3 to 14, unless taller than 1.5 metres, in which case they're treated as an adult regardless of age.
An adult may not occupy a seat without wearing a seatbelt, nor a seat on a row without seatbelts if a belted seat on that row is available.

A driver must ensure a child uses an appropriate child restraint where available, or a seatbelt if no restraint is available; if no belted seat is available and the vehicle has a rear seat, the child must sit there.
It is not compulsory to wear a seatbelt while reversing or moving in or out of a parking bay or area.
A motorcycle, tricycle, or quadrucycle rider and any passenger (including a sidecar passenger) must wear a properly fitted, purpose-designed protective helmet with the chin strap fastened.
A rider must ensure any passenger under 14 years old also wears a protective helmet.
A driver passing a stationary bus must do so with due care for people approaching or leaving it.
A vehicle must have an efficient exhaust silencer that channels exhaust gas through it.
Exhaust smoke may not be dense enough to be a nuisance, or to obstruct other road users' vision.
The exhaust may not be positioned where oil or flammable liquid could drip onto it, and may not leak gas or smoke into the cab or passenger compartment.
A light or heavy motor vehicle's engine must be covered so that it isn't a source of danger.
Heavy motor vehicles, goods vehicles, minibuses, and buses (but not motor cars, ambulances, or motorcycles) must carry at least one emergency warning triangle.
For a combination of vehicles, the warning triangle for each vehicle in the combination may all be carried on the drawing vehicle.
Don't give a hand signal on a freeway (except for reasons beyond your control), be on a freeway on foot, or leave an animal where it could stray onto one.

A stationary vehicle must place a warning triangle at least 45 metres away in the direction traffic will approach from, at roughly the same distance from the roadway edge as the vehicle's own centre, with the reflective side facing oncoming traffic.

A warning triangle isn't required if the vehicle is stopped in a loading zone, on a traffic officer's or sign's direction, because of other traffic while the driver stays in the driving seat, or during a state or municipal function.
A vehicle capable of reaching 60 km/h or more must be equipped with a working speedometer.
A general speed limit applies to all roads even without a sign: 60 km/h in urban areas, 100 km/h on non-freeway roads outside urban areas, and 120 km/h on freeways, unless a sign indicates otherwise.
Exceeding the applicable speed limit is an offence.
Buses and minibuses conveying persons for reward have a speed limit of 100 km/h.

An 80 km/h speed limit applies to a goods vehicle with a GVM over 9000kg, a combination where the combined GVM of the goods vehicle and trailer(s) exceeds 9000kg, an articulated vehicle whose truck-tractor GCM exceeds 9000kg, and any breakdown vehicle towing another vehicle.
A double-deck bus (with load) may not exceed 4.65 metres in height; any other motor vehicle may not exceed 4.3 metres.
A bus with a front wheel track over 1.9 metres may not exceed 2.6 metres overall width; a goods vehicle of 12,000kg GVM or more may not exceed 2.6 metres; any other vehicle may not exceed 2.5 metres.
Goods must be safely contained within, or securely fastened to, the vehicle, and protected from falling or spilling.
On a motor car's roof, goods may not exceed half the car's height measured from ground level, except pedal cycles.
A shipping container fitted with twist-lock provisions must be secured with at least four twist locks.
Baggage on a motorcycle should be placed in carriers securely attached to the motorcycle.
The section of a goods vehicle carrying persons must be enclosed to at least 350mm above a seated person, or 900mm above a standing person.
It is against the law for passengers to ride in a caravan.
A motorcycle's load (or sidecar load) may not project more than 600mm in front of the front axle, 900mm behind the rear axle, 450mm to either side, or 300mm beyond the sidecar wheel.

A light or heavy vehicle's goods may not project sideways from the centre-line by more than 1.3 metres (bus or goods vehicle over 12,000kg GVM) or 1.25 metres (any other vehicle), excluding mirrors or indicators.
A light or heavy vehicle's goods may not project more than 300mm beyond the front of the vehicle, or 1.8 metres beyond the rear.

A load projecting more than 150mm to the side, or 300mm to the rear, must be marked with a red flag (300mm x 300mm) during the day, and white (front) or red (rear) retro-reflectors at night or whenever visibility is poor.
On a public road divided into two or more roadways, drive only on the left-hand roadway, unless directed or permitted otherwise by a road traffic sign or a traffic officer.
Drive on the left side of the roadway, without encroaching right, unless it can be done safely or you're directed otherwise by a sign or traffic officer.
When another vehicle wants to pass you, keep as near to the left edge of the roadway as is safely possible, and don't speed up until it has passed.
When passing oncoming traffic, don't encroach onto the roadway to your right in a way that obstructs or endangers it.
Direction indicators must be used every time you turn left or right, or change lanes.

A light motor vehicle's indicators must flash intermittently, be clearly visible at 30 metres in daylight, and show white, yellow, or amber light to the front, and yellow, amber, or red light to the rear.
A motorcycle, motorcycle with sidecar, or motor tricycle must have a red retro-reflector fitted at the rear.
A light motor vehicle must have two red retro-reflectors at the rear, one on each side.
A heavy motor vehicle must have two red retro-reflectors at the same height at the rear, one on each side.

A heavy vehicle or combination longer than 7 metres must have yellow retro-reflectors along each side, spaced so no two successive ones are more than 3.6 metres apart, unless yellow reflective strips are fitted instead.
Since 1 January 2001, a goods vehicle with a GVM over 10,000kg must have yellow reflective material on its sides and rear; it's optional (but permitted) for vehicles under 10,000kg GVM.
Pass another vehicle on the right at a safe distance, and don't return to the left side until safely clear of the vehicle you passed.
Exceeding the speed limit while overtaking or passing is not permitted.
Passing may never be done by driving on the shoulder or the verge of a public road.

Don't pass other traffic when approaching the summit of a rise, a curve, or anywhere visibility is too restricted to see oncoming traffic, unless you can do so without encroaching right, or the road is restricted to one direction.
When another vehicle wants to pass you, keep left and don't accelerate until it has passed.
A learner's licence test covers rules of the road and related legislation, road traffic signs/signals/markings, and vehicle controls. Once passed, the learner's licence is valid for 24 months.

A person is disqualified from obtaining or holding a licence while addicted to narcotics or excessive alcohol use, while disqualified or suspended by a court or authority, or during a period following cancellation of a previous licence.
A person may not apply for a licence for a class of vehicle they are already licensed to drive under an existing licence.

A person is disqualified if suffering from uncontrolled epilepsy, disabling giddiness or fainting (e.g. from hypertension), a mental illness requiring detention or treatment, a condition causing muscular incoordination, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, defective vision below the prescribed standard, or any other disease or defect likely to prevent safe driving. Deafness alone is not disqualifying.
A Code 1 learner's licence authorises riding a motorcycle (but not a motor quadrucycle) on a public road. Minimum age is 16; under 18 you're limited to a 125cc engine; no passengers may be carried.
On a light or heavy motor vehicle, all lamps must be undamaged, unobscured, properly secured, and capable of being lit at all times.
These lighting rules don't apply to a vehicle parked off the roadway, in a demarcated parking place, or within 12 metres of a lit street lamp illuminating the road.
Every headlamp on main beam must adequately illuminate the road ahead, enabling the driver to see a person, vehicle, or substantial object at least 100 metres away.
A motorcycle's steering gear must be maintained so it can be steered safely and efficiently, and handlebar width and handgrip height must meet prescribed measurements based on engine capacity.
A vehicle's turning radius may not exceed 13.1 metres.
A light motor vehicle's windscreen must give the driver sufficient visibility for safe driving, be made of safety glass, and allow at least 70% light transmittance.
A light or heavy motor vehicle with a windscreen must have at least one wiper that continuously, evenly, and adequately clears the area directly in front of the driver.
A light or heavy vehicle may not have a bracket projecting more than 150mm beyond the vehicle's widest part (side mirrors and indicators excepted).
On a road divided into lanes by markings, don't change lanes unless it can be done without obstructing or endangering other traffic.
Before stopping or turning, give a clear, timely signal of your intention, long enough and visible enough to warn anyone approaching from the front, rear, or side.
A motor vehicle must be equipped with flasher-type direction indicators on both sides.
Don't park within 1.5 metres of a fire hydrant.
Outside an urban area, don't park on the roadway (excluding the shoulder), or with any part of the vehicle within 1 metre of the roadway edge, except for reasons beyond your control.
Don't stop on the roadway except to avoid an accident, on a traffic officer's direction, or for reasons beyond your control.
Don't deposit fuel, oil, grease, or other flammable or offensive matter on or alongside a road.
A motorcycle rider must obey every road sign and rule of the road, unless a traffic officer instructs otherwise.
A motorcycle may not be used to tow another vehicle.
Towing at over 30 km/h with a rope or chain is not allowed -- a draw-bar or tow-bar connection is required instead.
A towed vehicle may only carry passengers at over 30 km/h if it is a semi-trailer.
A motorcycle may not be fitted with a retreaded tyre.

Acceptable identification includes a South African ID document or card, a valid South African passport, a foreign ID or traffic register number certificate (for non-residents), or a driving licence card.
An articulated motor vehicle is a combination of a truck-tractor and a semi-trailer.
A licence disc is a disc issued under the Act that licenses a vehicle for use on a public road, valid for 12 months.
A midibus is a sub-category of bus designed to carry more than 16 and up to 35 people, including the driver.
A motorcycle is a motor vehicle with two wheels, including one with a sidecar attached.
A tractor is a motor vehicle designed mainly for drawing other vehicles with a GCM not exceeding 24,000kg; it does not include a truck-tractor.
A trailer is a vehicle not self-propelled, designed to be drawn by a motor vehicle, excluding a motorcycle sidecar.
A motor vehicle licence and licence disc are valid for 12 months from the first day of the month of issue; the expiry date is shown on both.
A driver wanting to overtake a vehicle ahead (not in the left lane) may signal their intention by flashing their headlights.
On a freeway, keep left and overtake on the right.

Within an urban area, don't park within 9 metres of the approach side of a pedestrian crossing, within 5 metres of an intersection, over a traffic signal's mechanism, more than 450mm from the kerb, on a road narrower than 5.5 metres, or on a traffic island, pedestrian mall, or pedestrian lane.
Obey every road traffic sign and rule of the road, unless a traffic officer instructs you otherwise.
A motorcycle with an engine over 50cc must have tyres showing a clearly visible tread pattern across the full breadth and circumference, at least 1mm deep.
A motorcycle with an engine of 50cc or under may not run a tyre with less than 80% visible tread pattern across the tread width.
If asked by someone with reasonable grounds, a driver must give their name and address, the vehicle owner's name and address, and the vehicle's registration number.
Except on a medical practitioner's instruction, a driver may not consume alcohol or narcotic drugs before reporting an accident.

If a person has been killed or injured and the accident fully obstructs the roadway, a vehicle may not be moved unless its position is clearly marked on the road, or a traffic officer authorises its removal.
A vehicle damaged in a collision may not be removed from the accident scene without the driver's or owner's permission.
Don't drive on a public road without reasonable consideration for other road users.
Don't drive recklessly or negligently, or in a manner that wilfully disregards the safety of people or property.
Don't drive with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05g per 100ml or more (0.02g per 100ml or more for a professional driver).
A bridge includes a culvert and a causeway.
A bus is a motor vehicle designed or adapted to carry more than 16 people, including the driver.
A combination of motor vehicles means two or more motor vehicles coupled together.
A dedicated lane is a portion of road reserved for certain periods for the exclusive use of certain vehicle categories, as shown by an appropriate sign.
A direction indicator is a device fitted to a vehicle allowing the driver to signal an intention to change direction left or right.
DLTC stands for Driving Licence Testing Centre, registered under the National Road Traffic Act.
If these details haven't already been given to a traffic officer at the scene, the accident must be reported to a police station within 24 hours, along with any further information required.
A driver is any person who drives or attempts to drive a vehicle, rides or attempts to ride a pedal cycle, or leads a draught, pack, or saddle animal, or a herd or flock of animals.
The edge of the roadway is the boundary between the roadway and the shoulder, as indicated by a sign, or otherwise the edge of the surfaced or improved part of the road.
A freeway is a public road, or section of one, designated as a freeway by an appropriate road traffic sign.
Goods means any movable property.

A goods vehicle is a motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle, tricycle, quadrucycle, motor car, minibus, or bus) designed to carry goods on a public road; it includes a truck-tractor, adaptor dolly, converter dolly, and breakdown vehicle.
Gross Combination Mass (GCM) is the maximum mass of a vehicle combination (including the drawing vehicle) and its load, as specified by the manufacturer or, failing that, the registering authority.
Gross Vehicle Mass (GVM) is the maximum mass of a vehicle and its load, as specified by the manufacturer or, failing that, the registering authority.
A haulage tractor is a motor vehicle designed mainly for drawing other vehicles, with a GCM exceeding 24,000kg; it does not include a truck-tractor or tractor.
An intersection is the area where two or more public roads open to vehicular traffic join or cross at any angle.
A minibus is a motor vehicle designed to carry more than nine but not more than 16 people, including the driver.
A motor car is a motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle, tricycle, or quadrucycle) designed to carry not more than nine people, including the driver.
A motor quadrucycle is a motor vehicle (other than a tractor) with four wheels, designed to be driven using motorcycle-type controls.
A motor tricycle is a motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle or tractor) with three wheels, designed to be driven using motorcycle-type controls.
A motor vehicle is any self-propelled vehicle, including a trailer and a pedal-and-motor vehicle designed to be propelled by pedals, an engine, or both.
A number plate is a prescribed plate displaying a vehicle's licence number or a motor trade number.
A pedestrian crossing is a portion of road designated as such by a sign, or, absent a sign, the portion at an intersection within the extension of the kerb line and adjacent boundary line.
A public road is any road, street, or thoroughfare commonly used by, or open to, the public, including its verge and any bridge, ferry, or drift it crosses.
A retro-reflector is a reflector complying with SABS specification 513, bearing a certification or approval mark.
A road traffic sign is a sign for prohibiting, limiting, regulating, or controlling traffic (in general or a particular class) on a public road.
The roadway is the portion of a road built or intended for vehicular traffic, between the edges of the roadway.
A semi-trailer is a trailer with no front axle, designed so at least 15% of its tare is borne by the vehicle drawing it.
The shoulder is the portion of road between the edge of the roadway and the kerb line.
Tare, for a vehicle, is its mass ready to travel on a road, including standard accessories and permanent structural parts, but excluding fuel.
A traffic island is a physical island that channels traffic within a junction or on a public road.
A traffic lane is a longitudinal division of a road wide enough for a single line of vehicles.
An urban area is a local authority area that has been surveyed and subdivided into erven, including the public roads bordering it.
A verge is the portion of a road, including the sidewalk, that is not the roadway or the shoulder.
LMV means Light Motor Vehicle -- tare/GVM not exceeding 3500kg.

HMV means Heavy Motor Vehicle -- tare exceeds 3500kg, or a minibus/bus/goods vehicle GVM exceeds 3500kg, or an articulated/combination vehicle's GCM (or trailer GVM) exceeds the prescribed thresholds.
MC means Motorcycle, and includes a motorcycle, tricycle, and quadrucycle.
After being involved in or contributing to an accident, a driver must stop immediately, check for and assist with any injuries, and assess the damage.
A driver may not hold a cellular or other communication device in one or both hands, or with any other part of the body, while driving.
Goods may not be loaded so that they touch the road surface, or obstruct the driver's view to the front, either side, or in the rear-view mirror.
No person may drive a motor vehicle on a public road except under a licence issued in terms of the National Road Traffic Act, and must keep that licence (or document) with them in the vehicle.
A licence to drive a motor vehicle is issued by a driving licence testing centre, and is either a provisional licence (a learner's licence) or a full driving licence.

A learner's licence application is made at a DLTC on form LL1, accompanied by two identical photos, acceptable identification (plus a copy), and the appropriate fee; applicants 65 or older must also submit a medical certificate (form MC) from a medical practitioner or occupational health practitioner.
A licence holder who permanently changes their place of residence must notify the registering authority of their new residential and postal address within 14 days.
An owner, operator, or person in charge of a vehicle may not employ or permit anyone to drive it on a public road unless that person is licensed to drive it.
To 'park' means to keep a vehicle stationary for longer than is reasonably necessary to load or unload people or goods, excluding delays beyond the driver's control.
The owner of a vehicle is responsible for all offences committed with it on a public road, if the owner permitted its use.
A motor vehicle may still be operated for up to 21 days after its licence expires (a 'period of grace'), provided the previous licence number and disc are displayed in the prescribed manner.
To 'cross' a public road means to move in a direction that intersects the normal course of travel of traffic on that road.
'Drawing' means towing a vehicle that is designed or adapted solely to be drawn, using a vehicle designed or adapted solely for that purpose -- as distinct from general 'towing'.
A driving licence card is a driving licence card issued in terms of the National Road Traffic Act.
'Driving time' is any period a driver occupies the driver's seat of a vehicle while it is being operated on a public road, or while the engine is running.
An emergency brake is a brake, other than the service brake, that is able to stop a vehicle.
The 'front end' of a vehicle is the part that projects furthest forward (for a semi-trailer, a line through the kingpin connecting the vehicle's widest point ahead of it).
An instructor is someone who, for direct reward, teaches another person to drive a motor vehicle, or teaches the rules of the road or road signs for a learner's or driving licence.
The kerb line is the boundary between the shoulder and the verge, or, where there's no shoulder, the boundary between the edge of the roadway and the verge.
A medical practitioner is a person registered as such under the Medical, Dental and Supplementary Health Service Professions Act.
To 'operate on a public road' means to use or drive a vehicle (or permit it to be used or driven), or to have or permit a vehicle to be on a public road.
Overall length is the distance between the front end and rear end of a vehicle, or (for a combination) between the front of the leading vehicle and the rear of the rearmost vehicle.
Overall height is the distance from ground level to the highest point of the vehicle or its load, excluding overhead electrical contacting gear or a catwalk on electrically driven vehicles.

Overall width is the distance between two planes parallel to the vehicle's centre-line, touching the widest projecting points on either side -- excluding side mirrors, direction indicators, or small fitments like air deflectors.
The 'owner' of a vehicle is the person with the right to use and enjoy it under common law or a contractual agreement, or a motor dealer in possession of it for sale.
A motorcycle's headlamp must be lit at all times when riding on a public road, day and night.
Headlamps, rear lamps, and number-plate lamps must be lit between sunset and sunrise, and at any other time when persons and vehicles aren't clearly visible at 150 metres.

A vehicle may not use an adjustable spot lamp on a public road, except official vehicles (ambulance, fire-fighting, police, traffic control), vehicles used by a medical practitioner or veterinarian for professional duties, or a breakdown vehicle or utility vehicle working at an accident, breakdown, or overhead line inspection.
A vehicle must be fitted with a rear-view mirror giving a clear view of traffic behind in clear weather (tractors are excepted).
A motor car, minibus, bus, or goods vehicle must have both an exterior mirror on the driving side and an interior mirror -- or two exterior mirrors if the interior one doesn't give a clear rear view.
Helmets aren't required if the motorcycle has SABS-compliant seatbelts and the engine cannot run unless the rider and any passenger are wearing them.

A vehicle may not be used if its fuel tank, carburettor, or fuel pipes are defective or exposed as a danger, if the fuel tank lacks an effective cap, or if the electrical wiring and battery aren't properly installed, insulated, and maintained.

Maximum vehicle lengths: 8 metres for a trailer (not semi-trailer) under 12,000kg GVM; 12.5 metres for one over 12,000kg GVM; 18.5 metres for an articulated motor vehicle; 22 metres for a bus-train or any combination of motor vehicles; 12.5 metres for any other vehicle.
The 'rear end' of a vehicle is the part that projects furthest to the rear.
'Roadworthy', for a vehicle, means it complies with the relevant legal provisions and is otherwise fit to be operated on a public road.
A service brake is a brake, normally a footbrake, used to reduce a vehicle's speed or bring it to a stop.
A sidewalk is the portion of a verge intended for the exclusive use of pedestrians.
'The Act' refers to the National Road Traffic Act, 1996 (Act No. 93 of 1996), which governs road traffic in South Africa.
'Towing' means towing a vehicle that is not designed or adapted solely to be drawn -- as distinct from 'drawing', which refers to vehicles built solely for that purpose.
At intersections, railway crossings and scholar patrols.
To bring traffic to a stop.

Bring your vehicle to a stop behind the stop line. If there is no stop line, the front of the vehicle must come to a stand still in line with the stop sign. At a three or four-way stop you may not move off before all the other vehicles which stopped before you have moved off. Proceed only when it is safe.
At the beginning of any road or part of a road.
Indicate that a road or part of a road may be used by motorcyclists only. Motorcyclists must follow the route indicated by the road traffic sign.
No driver of any other vehicle may use the road or part of the road indicated by this sign. Motorcyclists may use only that part of the road indicated by this sign.
On any road or at an entrance to a parking area.
To reserve a portion of a road or a parking area for use by delivery vehicles only.
Do not use this road or parking area if you are not driving a delivery vehicle.
On any road or at an entrance to a parking area.
To reserve a portion of a road or a parking area for use by abnormal vehicles only.
Do not use this road or parking area if you are not driving an abnormal vehicle.
On any road or at an entrance to a parking area.
To reserve a portion of a road or a parking area for use by high occupancy vehicles only.

Slow down and stop if a pedestrian is waiting at the crossing. Do not overtake other vehicles that have stopped at the pedestrian crossing.

Do not enter this area if you are driving a motorcar.
On any road.

Proceed only in the direction indicated by the arrow.

Make sure that the route you are travelling on is the route that you want to take to reach your destination.

Do not enter this area if you are driving animal-drawn vehicle.

Obey all other road traffic signs. Look out for vehicles, pedestrians and other hazards engaged in the experiment.

Be aware that buses may slow down and stop. Look out for pedestrians when overtaking

On any road or at an entrance to a parking area.

Slow down to avoid potholes without endangering other traffic.

Look out for elephants ahead and be prepared to slow down or stop.
On any road, especially in wildlife sanctuaries.
To warn that there is a possibility of warthogs being present on the road ahead.
Look out for warthogs ahead and be prepared to slow down or stop.
On any road, where the carriageway ends.

Decide which direction to go and slow down.
On any road close to water, harbours.
To warn that the road leads to a jetty edge or riverbank.
Slow down and look out for the end of the road so that you can stop in time.

Below a regulatory sign on any public road.

Obey the times on this sign.

Stop if the STOP sign is displayed and move off or proceed with caution if safe when the GO sign is displayed.

Approach cautiously, and yield to traffic approaching from left or right.
On any road before a intersection with traffic light.

Slow down immediately and be ready to stop if the light changes from green to amber. Make sure there are no pedestrians or cross-traffic who might not obey the signals.
At intersections.

Bring your vehicle to a standstill behind the stop line. If there is no stop line, the front of your vehicle must be brought to a stop in line with the stop sign. Proceed only when it is safe. If more than one vehicle stops at such an intersection, the vehicle, which stopped first, should move off first.
At intersections where a one-way road joins another road.
To indicate that there is a one-way carriageway to the left, right, or ahead.
Proceed in the direction of the arrow only if you want to use that specific carriageway.
On any road with more than one traffic lane in the direction you are travelling.
To warn that the double-lane road you are driving on narrows by a full lane from the left (W215 or TW215) or from the right-hand side (W214 or TW 214).
Depending on which sign is displayed, change in good time to the lane that carries on.
On any road before a intersection with a stop sign.
To warn that there is a stop sign ahead, which cannot be seen in time.
Slow down in good time and be ready to stop as required for sign R1.1.
On any road or at an entrance to a parking area.

Do not use this road or parking area if you are not driving a vehicle conveying hazardous substances.

To warn that pedestrians may be crossing the road for the next 2 km.
Slow down and look out for pedestrians who may be crossing the road.
On any road especially in mountainous areas.
To warn that there is a tunnel ahead.
Slow down and switch your car's headlights on in the dim position.
On the left and right-hand edge of the road.
To indicate where the left or right-edge of the road is.

Avoid driving to the left of the left-edge line. You may, however drive here only; whilst being overtaken by another vehicle, if you can so without endangering yourself, other traffic, pedestrians or property, during daytime and if persons and vehicles on the road are clearly discernible at a distance of at least 150 metres. It is not compulsory to drive to the left of the line when you are being overtaken, keep in mind that you have very little space when doing so. If your vehicle breaks down, stop as far left from the line as possible and switch on your emergency lights. The right-edge line is usually found on one-way roads such as dual carriageways or freeways and may not be crossed.
On any road.
To warn that there are speed humps on the carriageway ahead which require a reduction of speed.
Slow down so that you can drive over the speed humps without damaging your vehicle or losing control.
On any road.
To warn that there is a possibility of electrical shock from the overhead electrical power cables on the road ahead.
Look out for electrical cables on the road way ahead.
At intersections and pedestrian crossings
To compel you to give priority to pedestrians crossing the road or wanting to cross the road.
Look out for pedestrians crossing the road or near the road and be ready to stop.
At traffic circles, particularly mini circles.
To warn you that there is a traffic circle ahead where they must expect to yield.

Look out for other vehicles and yield to vehicles already in the circle or that will cross the yield line at their entrance to the circle before you will cross yours. Stop if necessary. The driver who reaches his/her yield line first may proceed first. At a mini circle you must, as at a normal intersection, signal in time in which direction you want to turn.
At intersections and railway crossings.
To indicate that you must yield to other traffic.
If other traffic is approaching the intersection, reduce speed and, if necessary, stop.
Usually found at the end of a one-way street, at the end of an off-ramp or at intersections where two-way traffic roads change to one-way traffic.
To indicate that no traffic may proceed past the sign on the road, carriageway or lane.
Do not enter the carriageway where this sign is displayed.
Especially in mountainous areas.

Slow down and, particularly in mountainous areas with sharp curves, be able to stop within the distance you can see. Remember to allow for a longer stopping distance on a descent especially when your vehicle is heavily laden.
At intersections.

If you intend to carry straight on, bring your vehicle to a standstill behind the stop line. When turning left, yield to all traffic, which is close enough to pose a hazard. Proceed only when it is safe.
At the entrance to any road intended for dual way traffic.
To indicate that there is a single carriageway ahead for use by vehicle from both directions.
Look out for other vehicles and yield to vehicles already in the carriageway.
On any road.

Slow down and adjust your position on the roadway.
On any road.
To warn that there is a possibility of congested traffic.
Look out for slow moving vehicle and adapt speed accordingly.
On any road before a railway crossings between the warning sign and the railway crossing.
To warn that there is a railway crossing ahead.
Slow down and if necessary, stop before the crossing.
On carriageways and at intersections where traffic moves in the same direction.
To prohibit you from crossing the line.
Drive in such a way that no part of your vehicle crosses the line.
On any road especially in rural areas.
To warn that tractors or other slow-moving agricultural vehicles could cross or enter the road ahead.
Look out for agricultural vehicles and slow down of they want to cross the road or are crossing it.
On any road where there is fog or smoke.
To warn that there is a possibility reduced visibility on the road ahead that might cause a hazard to road users.
Look out for Fog or smoke and slow down. Be on the look out for other slow moving vehicles.
On any road, especially in wildlife sanctuaries and rivers.
To warn that there is a possibility of hippos being present on the road ahead..
Look out for hippos ahead and be prepared to slow down or stop.
On any road.

Do not continue of your vehicle is wider than indicated on the sign.
On the left-hand side of any road where two routes join the numbered route by means of a set of one-way carriageways.

You need to know before hand in which direction you want to travel, e.g. North(N) or South(S).
Above the lanes most appropriate to the movement which is indicated.

Make sure which route you want to follow, slow down for the intersection and take the correct route.
At the intersection of toll and alternative routes.
To point out that a route other than the toll route can be followed.

Decide in advance whether you want to take the toll or alternative route. If you want to take the alternative route, slow down for the intersection. Remember that the alternative route is usually not of the same high standard as the toll route.
On any road.
To indicate to cyclists and other road users that there is a special route for cyclists only.
Do not use this route and look out for cyclists that could suddenly change direction to follow the cycle route.
On the opposite side of the intersecting cross road at the end of an off-ramp.
To indicate the direction of the various destinations at the end of a freeway exit (off-ramp).
Slow down and be ready to stop, turn left or right, depending on road traffic signs and signals and your destination.
On the far left-hand corner of an intersection.
To indicate the numbers of the routes leading from this intersection and destinations that can be reached from this intersection.
Slow down and make sure you take the correct route. Also look out for other traffic at the intersection that might not yield.
On the left-hand side or in an overhead position on a freeway, about 2 km before an off-ramp exit.
To indicate early on that there is an exit from the freeway to certain routes ahead.
If you want to leave the freeway, move to the left hand lane in good time.
On the left-hand side of a freeway, about 500m before an off-ramp exit.
To confirm early on that there is an exit from the freeway to certain destinations ahead.
If you want to leave the freeway, you should be in the extreme left hand lane by now.
On any road.

Be on the look out for approaching vehicles.
On the left-hand side of the road a short distance beyond an intersection.
To confirm the route to a destination and the distance indicated in kilometres to such destinations.
Note the destination and in particular note the distance to the destination so that you can plan your trip to fill up with petrol or rest.
In urban areas on the opposite side of an intersection near the street name sign or traffic light.
To indicate to drivers the route number of the class-B route.
Slow down for the intersection and make sure that you take the correct route.
On the left-hand side of a road.

Follow the traffic signs if you want to join the more important route and look out for the next trailblazer.
On any road with more than one traffic lane, especially in rural areas.
To inform in advance which lane leads to a specific destination.
Move in good time to the correct lane that leads to your destination or route.
On the left-hand side of any road which is not a freeway.
To point out the direction of a transport terminus from a route that would otherwise have taken you past a bus terminus, harbour, airport or helipad.
Follow the traffic signs if you want to go to the terminus and look out for the transport trailblazer that follows.
In an intersection.
To guide you to follow the correct route in the intersection.
Turn according to the markings.
Below a regulatory sign on any public road.
To limit the times and periods of stopping.
Do not stop or park for longer than the times indicated.

Look out for horses and riders ahead and be prepared to slow down or stop.

Do not pass to the right of W401 or TW401 and to the left of W402 or TW402
On any road especially in mountainous areas.

Slow down and look out for traffic that might not yield at the intersection.
On the left-hand side of an ordinary road.

Decide on the direction and route you want to follow and position your vehicle to join the on-ramp at the freeway or proceed straight ahead.
On the left-hand side of an ordinary road on the far side of an on-ramp.

Slow down and make sure you are in the right-hand lane if you want to join the freeway.
On any freeway.

Signal in time and make sure you are in the right-hand lane if you want to turn right to join the freeway.
On descents.
To indicate that there is an arrestor bed ahead and to indicate the entrance to such an arrestor bed.
Should the brakes of your vehicle fail, drive straight into the arrestor bed.
On any road.
To warn of a hazard ahead.
Slow down and look out for other road traffic signs that indicate a specific hazard.
At the beginning of any road or part of a road.

The driver of the taxi shall use that road.

Slow down enough to be able to round the curves safely or stop within the sight distance you can see.
On the left-hand side of the road.

If you are driving a heavy motor vehicle, engage a lower gear so that the vehicle will move down the descent more slowly. If the lower gear does not have the desired effect, engage an even lower gear to keep the speed constant and protect the brakes against overheating.

Whenever a lane ends, converges, merges or is added, make sure in time that there is a big enough gap in the traffic to merge with the traffic. Also yield to other traffic, which might merge.
On any road
To guide you by means of a diagram, which indicates that, a lane merges with another lane or that roadways join.
Whenever a lane ends, converges, merges or is added, make sure in time that there is a big enough gap in the traffic to merge with the traffic. Also yield to other traffic, which might merge.

Move to the correct lane in good time to turn left or right at the intersection..
On a multi-lane carriageway.
To warn that the traffic lanes are reduced from the left (WM6.1) or right (WM6.3) or from both (WM6.2) sides.
Change lanes in time if the lane you are travelling in ends. Check both the blind spots where two lanes end from both sides to make sure there is no other vehicle that is also changing lanes.
Displayed on the left-hand side of any road.
To inform you that the road ahead or the road to the left or right ends.
Do not turn in at such a road unless you are going to a destination in the road that ends.
At the entrance to a parking area.
To inform you of the existence of a park-and-ride terminus that has a bus (IN9) or train (IN10) service.
Stop in this parking area if you want to reach your destination using other transport.
On any public road, lane, path or area.

Do not enter this area if you are driving a tour bus.
Next to the entrance of a parking area or in the top right-hand or top left-hand corner of a notice board.
To inform you of the existence of an information office or notice board.
You can obtain information about the area at this sign.
On the left-hand side of the carriageway before an intersection.
To inform you that the traffic signals on this route are co-ordinated and that the signals will be green at all the subsequent intersections if you maintain the indicated speed.

If possible maintain the recommended speed. However, make sure that it is safe to enter every intersection and look out for drivers that do not yield. The speed indicated is a recommendation and not a speed limit.
At intersections at the same pole as traffic signals (robot) under signal head.

At a normal intersection you would expect that the signal in your direction will change to green after the signal for cross traffic was yellow. Do not move off when approaching traffic moves off. Wait until the signal is green. The sequence of the traffic signals at this intersection can be different during normal and during peak times.
On the left-hand side of any road.
To show that there is a transport modal transfer point or terminus nearby where passengers may change their mode of transport.
Make sure that it is safe to slow down and stop to drop someone off or pick someone up. Also look out for pedestrians who may cross the road.
On any road that carries two-way traffic (traffic from opposite directions).
To inform that it is prohibited to drive with any part of your vehicle on the right-hand side of this line.

Do not cross the line, except to gain direct access to an entrance on the other side of the line, to gain direct access from such an entrance to the road or to pass a stationary obstruction. In all these cases you must ensure that it is safe to do so.

To inform you that priority must be given to pedestrians crossing or wanting to cross the road at these places.
Look out for any pedestrians crossing or wanting to cross the road and give them priority by slowing down or stopping.
In urban areas.
To warn that one-way street you are driving on will soon be crossed by a street that carries two-way traffic.

If you are driving in the left hand lane and want to turn to the right at the first intersection, change to the right hand lane in good time. If you are driving in the right hand lane and wish to turn to the left at the first intersection, change to the left hand lane in good time.
At the beginning of any road or part of the road.

To indicate that a road or part of a road may be used by cyclists and/or pedestrians only. To indicate to cyclists and pedestrians which part of a road they must use. Signs R113 and TR115 indicate that part of the road is divided and that part may be used by cyclists and pedestrians only. A certain part may be used by cyclists or by pedestrians only, as indicated by the road traffic sign.

Do not drive on this road or part of this road. Cyclists and pedestrians may use only that part of the road indicated by these signs. Where this part of the road is divided, cyclists may use the part indicated on the sign by a bicycle symbol. Pedestrians may use the part indicated on the sign by a pedestrian symbol.
In areas where there is mining and industrial activities taking place.
Indicates that the road or a portion of the road is set aside for use by abnormal vehicles.
The driver of an abnormal vehicle shall only use such road or portion of such road.
On any public road, especially in mountainous areas.
To prohibit long vehicles from using a road where such a vehicle will not be able to negotiate a curve or will turn in such a manner that it will disrupt or endanger other traffic.
If applicable, take an alternative route.
At the beginning of and at entrances to any carriageway, lane or path.
To prohibit pedestrians from proceeding past this sign where they could cause a danger to themselves and to vehicles.
Despite the fact that pedestrians are prohibited on such a road, you must still look out for them. Pedestrians may not enter or cross a road where this sign is displayed.
On any public road, lane, path or area.
Indicates to the driver of a vehicle that no vehicle which is towing another vehicle shall proceed beyond such sign.
Do not enter this area if you are towing another vehicle or trailer.
On any road or other area where parking bays are demarcated.

Sign (R305-P) indicates a parking area for vehicles with a GVM of less than 3 500 kg where no time limit applies but a fee must be paid. Sign (R306-P) indicates a parking area that may be used free of charge or at a fee and the maximum time allowed for a vehicle to be parked, is displayed.
Park in accordance with the road traffic sign and road traffic markings. If necessary pay the tariff and do not park for longer than the time indicated.
On any public road especially in mountainous areas.
To warn of a series of curves ahead. In the case of W209 the first curve is to the left and in the case of W208 the first bend is to the right.
Slow down e3nough to take the curves safely or stop within the distance you can see. Remember that there could be any number of curves after the first one without further warning.
On any road before you reach the place where two roads join your road within a short distance.

To warn that your road is first joined by another road from the left hand side first and within a short distance by another from the right hand side (W110,TW110) or from the right first and then from the left (W109,TW109).
Slow down and be prepared to stop or turn at a safe speed. Look out for traffic at the intersection that might not yield.
On any road but especially in mountainous areas.
To warn that curves in the road or other structures on the side of the road make it impossible for vehicles longer than the length indicated on this road sign.
Find an alternative route if your vehicle is longer that the length indicated in metres on this sign.
On any road but especially in mountainous areas.
To warn that the road will climb or descend steeply.
Be aware of slow-moving traffic, particularly in mountainous areas with sharp curves. Allow for a longer stopping distance on a descent and especially when your vehicle is heavily laden.
On any road
To inform you by means of a diagram that the number of lanes of the road which you are travelling on will be increased soon. Opposing traffic flow is indicated by a dotted arrow.
Whenever a lane ends, converges, merges or is added, make sure in time that there is a big enough gap in the traffic to merge with the traffic. Also yield to other traffic, which might merge.
On any public road.
To warn that one or more concealed driveways enter the road you are driving on from the left or right in such a way that you cannot easily see the road or traffic travelling on that road.

Slow down so that you can stop or yield if there is cross traffic that do not yield at the intersection. Remember that a driver of such a vehicle that joins your road from the concealed driveway sometimes finds it also difficult to see you.
Especially in mountainous areas.
To warn that rocks could fall on the carriageway from the left (W334, TW334) or from the right-hand side (W335, TW335).

Slow down to be able to stop within their sight distance if a fall occurs or has occurred. Such falls occur more often when it rains and therefore reduce your speed further since your stopping distance during rainy weather will be longer.
On any road.
To warn that there is danger of some kind ahead.
Slow down and look out for anything on or next to the carriageway that could cause you to change speed or direction.
Where traffic density can be better controlled by traffic lights at intersections, junctions, pedestrian crossings, etc.
To regulate traffic coming from different directions.

These lights must be obeyed at all times in the following manner: Red - Stop. Flashing red arrow to the left - After stopping, the driver may turn if there is no traffic. Remember to yield to pedestrian traffic and oncoming traffic that wants to turn right, and traffic from the right passing through the intersection. Amber - Stop, except where it cannot be done safely. Constant amber arrow - Stop and wait until the flashing green arrow shows you may go. Green - Go if it is safe. Flashing green arrows - Right of way in the direction of the flashing arrow. Constant green arrow - Shows the direction in which traffic must go, for example one-way streets. Flashing amber disc - Drive on carefully, but yield to pedestrians. Pedestrians may cross the roadway. Flashing red signal - Indicates that the driver must stop and may carry on when it is safe (as at stop sign). At a railway crossing a flashing red light indicates that a train is coming and you may not drive on until the light stops flashing. (Red) figure light signal. Shows pedestrians that they may not cross the road until the green figure light signal is shown. If this sign flashes pedestrians who have not entered the roadway must wait until a green figure light signal shows. Pedestrians who are already in the intersection must cross the intersection as quickly as possible.
On any road.
To warn about a temporary stop sign, a collision scene, roadblock or similar scene where police are on duty.
Be ready to stop at the stop sign that follows after the flashing blue light or on demand of a police officer.
On any road.

To warn the driver that - the road ahead may be obstructed, there could be pedestrians, rescue teams and police or traffic officers controlling the traffic at the scene, there could be wreckage, injured persons, animals or broken glass on the road surface.

Slow down immediately, look out for someone controlling the traffic and be ready to stop. If there is enough or professional help on the scene, do not stop out of curiosity. Do not look at the collision scene or wreckage, concentrate on the route to be followed without driving over or into anything.
On any road before you reach the place where another road joins your road from the left (W107) (TW107) or from the right (W108) (TW108).
To warn that traffic may be approaching you from the left or right-hand side.
Slow down so that you will be able to stop, or go around the corner or pass the intersection at a safe speed. Look out for other traffic at the intersection that might not yield.
On any public road.
To warn that there is a traffic circle ahead where you may need to yield to other traffic.

Slow down so that you can stop or drive around the circle at a safe speed. Look out for road traffic signs and markings which will tell you whether you have the right of way or whether you have to yield. If there is no indication you have to give way to traffic approaching from the right. Vehicles within a traffic circle have right of way. If you have right of way still look out for traffic in the circle which may not yield to you. If sign R2.2 is displayed at the traffic circle, you must yield to any driver who crosses his yield line first before you cross yours.
On any road near schools.
Indicate that there is a scholar patrol operating ahead.
Slow down and look out for a stop sign displayed by the scholar patrol. Look out at all times for children who may suddenly cross the road.
